title: Post Patch Clamp Slice Fixation
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bg5tjy6n
materials: 1000 µl pipette tip (Rainin GP-L1000F or equivalent)
RP0235 Patch-Seq Internal Solution with Biocytin
Warning: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what PPE you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Materials
steps.instruction: Gather all necessary reagents and prepare the workspace.

substeps.instruction: Obtain tissue slices prepared following SOP AF0099 (mouse) or PF0295 (human).
Obtain fresh 4% PFA/2.5% Glutaraldehyde (per SOP RP0229) and fresh PBS (per SOP RP0001).
Fill an ice bucket with wet ice to keep the Biocytin Solution chilled.
Prepare a 3 ml plastic Pasteur pipette (BD Falcon 357575) by cutting off the tip.

steps.title: Prepare Fixation and Wash Plates
steps.instruction: Label and fill 24-well plates for fixation and PBS washing.

substeps.instruction: Label a 24-well plate (without insert) as “EPhys_YYMMDD_plate#” and place it in the AirClean hood for PFA/Glut fixation.
Ensure human tissue is assigned to a separate PFA/Glut plate, labeled with a note for human tissue only.
Fill each well of a second 24-well plate (with plate insert) with ~1 ml 1X PBS(-), filling through the insert to ensure proper filling.
Label the insert with the plate name “EPhys_YYMMDD_plate#” on the flat edge.
Ensure human tissue is assigned to a separate PBS plate from mouse tissue.

steps.title: Prepare Biocytin Internal Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare the Biocytin mix if pre-made solution is not available.

substeps.instruction: Obtain Internal Solution from the -20ºC freezer.
Weigh 4 to 5 mg of Biocytin powder into a microfuge tube using a balance.
Add the required volume of Internal Solution to achieve the desired concentration (e.g., for a 1% mix, add 420 µl of Internal Solution to 4.2 mg of Biocytin).
Vortex the tube until the Biocytin is completely dissolved.
Store the tube in the ice bucket with the lid closed.

steps.title: Extract Cell from Slice
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the recording pipette from the neuron following electrophysiology recording (SOP PF0301).

substeps.instruction: Pull the pipette away from the cell diagonally until a GΩ seal forms.
Switch the control cube to the “Approach” setting.
Slowly pull away from the cell in the X direction.
Move the index finger counter-clockwise in the control cube grooves, completing roughly one revolution every five seconds.
If finished patching in the slice, remove the harp from on top of the cell and allow the cell to rest for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Fix Slices
steps.instruction: Transfer the slice to the fixation solution and store.

substeps.instruction: Fill an empty well of the appropriate (mouse or human) PFA/Glut plate with ~500 µl of 4% PFA/2.5% Glutaraldehyde.
Use the Pasteur pipette to transfer the slice from the stage to the well.
Write the specimen ID and initials on the lid of the PFA/Glut plate above the corresponding well.
At the end of the recording day, place the PFA/Glut plate on the orbital shaker tray in the 4°C fridge.
For human tissue recorded after hours, keep the plate in the 4°C fridge at all times, removing it only for slice transfers.

steps.title: Transfer Slices to PBS
steps.instruction: Move fixed slices to PBS for long-term storage.

substeps.instruction: After slices have fixed for 2 days (>40 hours), transfer them from the PFA/Glut plate to the corresponding well in the PBS plate.
Note: Slices can be transferred up to four days later without issue.
Ensure all slices are adequately submerged in PBS.
Empty the PFA/Glut plates into the PFA waste bottle in the AirClean hood using a funnel.
